_comment: L1 deterministic-check config. Universal stuff (power-symbol filter, refdes pattern, missing-value sentinels, grid) lives in conventions.json — this file holds only the bits unique to checking.

reference._comment: Refdes annotation + format severities. The valid format itself comes from conventions.json:refdes.pattern. unannotated_pattern catches symbols KiCad has not yet given a number to (e.g. 'R?', 'U??').

value._comment: Severity for blank/placeholder Value fields. The placeholder list itself is conventions.json:missing_value_sentinels.

label._comment: Net-name rules. KiCad allows wide UTF-8 in labels but most tools (including KiCad ERC) prefer the strict pattern. Adjust if your project uses Unicode net names.
label._valid_pattern_comment: Allows leading digits (3V3, 12V, 1V8 are universal voltage-rail names) and KiCad bus/group {...} annotations. Disallows whitespace + most punctuation.
label._orphan_comment: Disabled by default ([] kinds). The simple count is fundamentally noisy: a label appearing once is fine when its wire connects to a component pin, sheet pin, or connector — the second endpoint is the pin, not another label. Proper detection needs net-walking (planned). Re-enable by setting orphan_kinds_to_check to e.g. ['label','global_label'] if you want best-effort flagging.
label._special_label_names_comment: Labels that always appear singly by design and should never be flagged as orphans (used only when orphan_kinds_to_check is non-empty).

grid._comment: Off-grid endpoints silently fail to connect in KiCad. Grid step itself is in conventions.json:grid.schematic_mm. Set check_components/check_labels/check_wire_endpoints to false to suppress a category.

geometry._comment: Visual cleanliness checks: no diagonal wires, no wires lying on top of each other, no labels stacked at one point, no symbols crammed on top of each other. Each check has its own severity + on/off toggle. Thresholds are in mm; defaults align with KLC + KiCad library convention.

wire_orthogonality._comment: Diagonal wire segments (KLC + KiCad convention forbid them). Disable only for special-purpose schematics that legitimately use diagonals.

wire_overlap._comment: Two wire segments lying on the same horizontal/vertical line and sharing more than one point. Causes ambiguous junction logic and ERC noise. Tolerance allows for floating-point grid drift.
wire_overlap._overlap_min_mm: Minimum overlap length to flag (avoids reporting two wires that merely touch at one endpoint).

label_collision._comment: Two labels at the same coordinate with different net names = ambiguous net binding. Same-name labels at the same point are redundant but harmless (kept off by default; flip flag_redundant to enable).

symbol_proximity._comment: Coarse origin-distance proxy. Superseded by symbol_bbox_overlap (which uses real lib_symbol body bboxes). Kept here for projects with heavy custom libraries where bbox parsing fails — re-enable manually if bbox check returns nothing.

symbol_bbox_overlap._comment: Real bbox-vs-bbox intersection between two placed components on the same sheet. Each component's body bbox comes from its lib_symbol primitives (rectangle/polyline/circle/arc, pins excluded per KLC S3.5). Symbols whose lib_id is not in lib_symbols (or has no body primitives) fall back to a square of fallback_size_mm centred on origin so they still get checked. min_overlap_area_mm2 ignores microscopic intersections from floating-point grid drift.

wire_through_body._comment: Per KLC S3.5: pins are placed OUTSIDE the symbol body and wires must NOT need to cross the body to reach a pin. We compute each placed component's body bbox from its lib_symbol primitives (rectangle/polyline/circle/arc, EXCLUDING pin shapes per KLC), then test every wire segment for true interior crossing. interior_margin_mm shrinks the bbox so floating-point grid drift on a boundary-touching wire (= legitimate pin tip) isn't flagged. min_body_dim_mm excludes tiny markers (test points, mounting holes, fiducials) where the body is just a marker around the pin — wires ending at such a pin would falsely look like they enter the body.

net_dangling_label._comment: Net-aware orphan-label check, powered by the union-find walker in nets.py. A label is dangling when its net has fewer than min_endpoints electrical members (pins + power ports).
net_dangling_label._disabled_default_reason: DEFAULT-DISABLED ([] kinds_to_check) until cross-sheet hierarchical-label binding ships. Per-sheet, labels that propagate to other sheets via sheet pins (e.g. 'PC-CLOCK-OUT' → parent connector J1 on a different sheet) appear as 0-endpoint nets and false-positive. Re-enable once nets.py walks sheet pins across the hierarchy. Set kinds_to_check to ['label','global_label'] to opt in for flat single-sheet projects.

junction_missing._comment: Per KLC CON_003: three or more wires meeting at a point must show an explicit junction dot. Without the junction, KiCad treats them as visually crossing but NOT electrically connected — silent net split. We count distinct wire segments that pass through each candidate point and flag points with >= 3 segments where no (junction) sexp exists.

label_over_wire._comment: A label's text must not visually overlap a wire it is NOT bound to (the bound wire IS supposed to pass through the anchor — that is the binding mechanism). Text bbox is estimated per KLC S3.2: text height = 1.27 mm (50 mil); char width = 0.6 × height (KiCad stroke font ratio).
label_over_wire._lift_comment: Vertical offset between the label anchor (which sits ON the bound wire) and the text bbox above it. KiCad's default label_offset_ratio = 0.15 of text height = ~0.19 mm; we use 0.25 mm as a safe halo that keeps the bound wire out of the bbox.
label_over_wire._min_overlap_mm: Ignore overlaps shorter than this (avoids false flags from text barely touching a wire endpoint).

functional._comment: L3 functional checks — uses nets.build_project_nets to reason about electrical topology, not just geometry. Each rule maps to a KLC rule_id where applicable.

missing_decoupling._comment: KLC POWER_001: every IC power-input pin must have a decoupling capacitor on the SAME net. We walk every net containing an IC power_in pin and check whether any capacitor (refdes prefix in cap_prefixes) is also a member. Excludes power-port-only nets (raw rails like a battery/regulator output before any caps) — those are caught by ERC PWR_FLAG checks instead.
missing_decoupling._ic_categories: Categories from conventions.json:refdes that are checked. 'ic' is the universal one; add transistors/connectors here only if your shop convention requires decoupling on those too.
missing_decoupling._cap_prefixes: Refdes letter codes that count as a decoupling capacitor. Just C by IEEE 315; some shops add CN/CC for special types.
missing_decoupling._pin_types: KiCad pin electrical_type values that need decoupling. power_in covers VCC/VDD/AVDD; bidirectional is excluded (those are signal pins).
missing_decoupling._skip_pin_names: Pin names that are pure ground and never need their own decoupling. Case-insensitive substring match.
missing_decoupling._min_pins: Skip ICs with fewer than this many pins total — single-pin parts (test points, connectors) often look like ICs by refdes but aren't real ICs.
